additional_info.subject: ID0444030-DC/Si-D/CH-[MP / R7 170002201]Charger issue CRM:02681000640
additional_info.body:
Hi Alexander! Good morning, how are you doing today?
I checked this charger and found the error:
This happened 2 times, during charging and during CableCheck.
We need to understand where the root cause lies, I suspect one of 3 bad guys:
Since we are in v6, when we are single charging (there is no parallel charging), the Feedback is acknowledged by the Voltage Transducer where he measures the busbar and says "yes I have voltage = fbk:ON"
One of the first things to check is if this connector can be loose, these can get loose very easily with vibrations:
Here we can also measure this value 2...10V OUT while charging and when the error occurs, records the multimeter values:
If we lose the voltage in XD41, then that means that the QA21-22 is not closing physically, if we have crocodile tips, we can measure directly on the busbar to be 100% sure it's the contactor fault and can replace it.
If we have voltage in XD41 but the session closes then we need to see where it drops until the KF7.
The third bad guy is the KF14. There are some rare events where the StateMonitor which is the responsible for closing the QA21-22, doesn't work properly and the feedback is always OFF. This one has no chance of troubleshooting, except replacing.
I recommend you to bring a spare TF1, KF14 and QA21-22. My recommendation is to start with the previous order of components from easiest to hardest.
I will send this to RC-CH queue for follow up. If you need my support please schedule with at least 2 days in advance as we are facing a lot of tickets these past days.
Let me know if everything was understood correctly, you can ping me via Teams if you have any doubts.
Thank you very much!
Best regards,
Francisco

Good day,
I have checked all the points in the ticket and could not find any errors or defects. At the TF1 output, we can measure >4 V (see video in the case).
All connections and terminals are correct and show no signs of corrosion.
The charger is charging the vehicles with the required power!
Would you like help drafting this as a formal update for a customer or internal report?
Br Simon
